title: Lifting against a two-term disk detects top-degree surjectivity
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $K,C,E$ be nonnegative chain complexes of $\Lambda$-modules, with chain maps as defined in [lem-cbc-dold-kan-normalization-equivalence]. Let $g:C\to E$ be a chain map and let $n\geq1$. Define $D^n$ to be the chain complex freely generated by $e_n$ in degree $n$ and $e_{n-1}$ in degree $n-1$, zero in all other degrees, with $\partial e_n=e_{n-1}$ and all other differentials zero. Let $j:K\to K\oplus D^n$ be the summand inclusion. Then $g_n:C_n\to E_n$ is surjective if and only if for every pair of chain maps $u:K\to C$ and $v:K\oplus D^n\to E$ with $gu=vj$, there exists a chain map $h:K\oplus D^n\to C$ satisfying $hj=u$ and $gh=v$ (the right lifting property of $g$ against $j$).
